note: Swapped two live configured options. Stash application invoked the other value's callback five times. raw() retains the address cached before the move.

note: A conflicting merge normally returned a conflicted index; enabling only skip_reuc returned MergeConflict (-24). The setter uses GIT_MERGE_FAIL_ON_CONFLICT.

note: Confirmed two configured helper entries supplying username and password separately; execute returned None. A single helper supplying both succeeded. Discovery uses single-value getters.

note: A local helper requiring a host field succeeded for a domain URL but returned None for IPv4 and IPv6 URLs. Source retains only Host::Domain.

note: Lookup of an existing lib.rs entry succeeded; ./lib.rs panicked through path_to_repo_path(...).unwrap() instead of producing an optional lookup result.

note: Sampled unsafe boundaries lack local explanations. Comment omissions and diagnostic counts do not establish additional incorrect behavior.

note: Source confirms broad allowances and generated methods allowing missing_docs. This is lint-policy and documentation housekeeping.

note: Normal safe checkout rejected a local-change conflict; dry_run returned Ok. The implementation selects GIT_CHECKOUT_NONE, which suppresses processing, rather than native DRY_RUN.

note: Calling dry_run().force() then checking out a tree created no file. force clears only low strategy bits and leaves the high GIT_CHECKOUT_NONE bit enabled.

note: Confirmed all four reported zero/default predicates return false and SHARED_GROUP.is_shared_all() returns true. The shared helper uses intersects for zero and composite values.

note: A promised GET followed by 103 and 200 panicked at counts.rs:111. ReservedRemote persists after 103, causing double counting; the assertion is unconditional.

note: A 16-byte padded frame delivered one body byte and reported only one used byte. Releasing it produced no WINDOW_UPDATE; the unpadded control passed. The shortened payload size also feeds connection accounting.

item: 304 responses reject empty final DATA
note: 304 with Content-Length: 100 followed by empty END_STREAM DATA returned PROTOCOL_ERROR. The same response ending in HEADERS passed; Remaining(100) incorrectly survives the header exemption.

item: Large capacity reservations truncate
note: After reserving 65,535 bytes, reserve_capacity(1usize << 32) reduced capacity to zero without sending data or allocating a large buffer. The unchecked u32 conversion cancels the reservation.

note: A valid HEAD promise followed by headers-only 200 with Content-Length: 100 returned PROTOCOL_ERROR. Promise processing never initializes ContentLength::Head, unlike ordinary HEAD requests.

item: All-target Clippy fails on the supplied toolchain
note: Reproduced eight Clippy errors promoted by the library-test deny(warnings). These are lint-cleanliness issues. The baseline build, 419 library tests, and 173 integration tests passed.

note: Strict private-item rustdoc reproduced bare-URL errors here and at frame/headers.rs:959. Strict public all-feature documentation passed. This is documentation formatting housekeeping.

note: A bounded writer returned zero once and a sentinel error next. Server handshake performed two writes and returned the sentinel instead of WriteZero. Source retries the unchanged buffer; no unbounded polling test was performed.

note: A scratch example following the guide failed with E0599. Changing poll_close to poll_closed compiled. Several guide references repeat the incorrect method name.

note: RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo test --locked -p h2-tests --no-run reproduced four deprecated std::usize diagnostics before tests compiled. Ordinary integration tests passed; this is build-cleanliness housekeeping.

note: With max_header_list_size(64), a checksum trailer containing a 100-byte value returned Ok(Some({})). Trailer handling ignores the decoder's oversize marker and successfully exposes the truncated fields.

note: A response HEADERS block containing only content-length: 0 returned a successful HTTP 200 response. Conversion leaves Response::builder's default status when the mandatory pseudo-header is absent.

note: The 42-byte decoded :status: 200 block failed with PROTOCOL_ERROR at limit 42 and passed at 43. Both pseudo-header and ordinary-field comparisons incorrectly require size strictly below the maximum.

note: A transport read returning OS error 5 produced an h2 connection error whose get_io().raw_os_error() was None. Internal conversion retains only ErrorKind and optional text, also destroying typed inner errors.

note: The Error trait implementation uses the default source() returning None. Adding chaining is a public-API improvement without a documented chaining contract; get_io()/into_io() already provide explicit I/O access. Original-error destruction is assessed separately.

note: One rejected POST push increased stored streams from one to two; the extra entry remained after parent completion and acceptance of the next request. A forbidden connection-header control cleaned up correctly. The early ? bypasses child removal; no resource-exhaustion investigation was performed.

note: Independent two-thread regression passed natively; Miri detected a data race at spsc.rs:273. Availability checks use relaxed loads without acquiring publication.

note: After rotating and compacting a full capacity-four deque, removing all four elements leaves len=4 and is_empty=false. The branch assigns back=capacity.

note: Changing 2 to 20 and popping returns 20 but leaves [20,3], losing 1. pop leaves maybe_changed armed for the destructor's second removal.

item: BufMut rejects valid exact-capacity writes
note: Independent owned-vector put_slice and vector-view put_u8 tests panic when filling advertised remaining capacity. advance_mut incorrectly rejects equality with capacity.

item: Vec owning iterator repeats destruction after panic
note: Counter regression observed [2,2,2] destruction counts, including an already-consumed element. A destructor panic bypasses clearing the backing vector's length.

item: Deque clear retains ownership during panicking destruction
note: After catching a destructor panic in clear and dropping the deque, counters were [2,2,2]. Empty-state bookkeeping occurs after destruction.

item: HistoryBuf clear retains ownership during panicking destruction
note: After catching a destructor panic in clear and dropping the buffer, counters were [2,2,2]. Length bookkeeping still describes the destroyed elements.

item: IndexMap truncation breaks retained-key lookup
note: Inserting u32 keys [0,1,5] and truncating to two retains key 0 in iteration but get(&0) returns None. Clearing slots leaves broken probe chains.

item: LinearMap collection bypasses duplicate-key replacement
note: Collecting [(1,10),(1,20)] produces two entries and returns 10 on lookup. Capacity one panics despite only one distinct key; FromIterator directly extends storage.

item: resize_default clones a single default and initializes while shrinking
note: Growing Rc<Cell<u8>> vectors creates shared cells. A separate shrinking regression invokes a panicking Default. Both follow from delegating to resize(new_len,T::default()).

item: CString constructor accepts missing nul termination
note: Both b"abc" and empty input return Ok, contradicting the explicit missing-terminator error contract. The constructor delegates to permissive append.

item: Owning IndexMap iteration reverses insertion order
note: Independent regression observed [3,2,1] after inserting [1,2,3]. IntoIter pops the final bucket, reversing the ordered map's borrowed iteration order.

item: IndexMap retain leaves stale indices after predicate panic
note: After removing 0 and panicking on 1, iteration contains [1,2], get(&1) returns None, and get(&2) panics on the stale index assertion. Rebuilding is skipped during unwinding.

item: IndexMap accepts capacities exceeding its packed entry indices
note: A capacity-131072 map accepted 65537 entries and reported that length, but lookup of 65536 returned None. Entry indices decode through u16; constructors lack a corresponding limit.

item: LinearMap implements Eq without requiring Eq values
note: LinearMap<u8,f32,1> satisfies a generic Eq bound while a map containing NaN compares unequal to itself. The implementation requires only V:PartialEq.

item: VecView lacks Serde serialization support
note: An independent compile probe accepts the owned vector but rejects as_view() with E0277. Serialize's storage parameter has an implicit Sized bound.

item: Strict Clippy fails on the installed toolchain
note: Reproduced strict Clippy failure: 13 library errors and 17 including library tests. These are lint-cleanliness diagnostics on Rust 1.99.1, not behavioral defects.

item: Conversion and extension panic/error documentation is incomplete
note: Representative collection implementations unwrap capacity failures without local panic documentation. Missing headings and documentation are hygiene under the requested classification.

item: Public entry handles and SPSC endpoints lack Debug
note: Source confirms representative Entry, Consumer, and Producer types lack Debug implementations. This is public-API diagnostic convenience, not incorrect behavior.

item: Unsafe operations lack some local invariant explanations
note: Representative unsafe implementations omit local justification of trait invariants. Comment coverage is documentation housekeeping; actual synchronization defects are assessed separately.

item: Lint suppressions lack structured reasons
note: Source contains allow(unused) and allow(private_bounds) attributes without reason fields. This is suppression-documentation style.

item: OccupiedEntry key returns the lookup key instead of the stored key
note: Using keys equal by ID but carrying different labels, occupied-entry key() returns "query" while the stored key is "stored". It references the retained query field.

item: HistoryBuf clone leaks completed clones when a later clone panics
note: A drop-counter regression observed zero cleanup calls for the completed first clone after the second clone panicked. Destination ownership metadata remains empty until the loop finishes.

item: docsrs configuration uses a removed nightly feature
note: Reproduced E0557 for doc_auto_cfg on nightly-2026-10-01. This is release/toolchain compatibility; ordinary documentation with warnings denied builds successfully.

item: HistoryBuf new_with permits unusable zero capacity
note: HistoryBuf::<u8,0>::new_with(42) constructs successfully, then oldest() panics indexing an empty buffer. Unlike new(), new_with lacks the nonzero-capacity assertion.

item: Formatting multiline module documentation corrupts source
note: A valid multiline doc attribute was overwritten as a comment followed by bare text. Formatting returned success; reparsing failed.

item: Invalid datetime function formats panic
note: datetime('%Q') and datetime_utc('%') each exited 101 with an uncaught Display formatting panic.

item: Invalid timestamp option formats panic
note: --timestamp --timestamp-format %Q exited 101 before executing the recipe. This configuration formatting path needs separate error handling.

item: Ambiguous external module directories panic
note: An external directory containing justfile and .justfile caused a StripPrefixError panic and exit 101. The equivalent local ambiguity returned a normal diagnostic.

item: Formatting drops eager assignment evaluation
note: With set lazy, an eager backtick assignment initially exited 42. Formatting removed eager; the same recipe subsequently succeeded.

item: Inherited bindings take precedence over local declarations
note: Local references printed the predefined HEX value despite its redefinition, and a child reference used the parent's x. Recursive scope lookup precedes local assignment evaluation.

item: Source caching conflates module identities and overrides
note: Two modules loading one file executed only b once. Distinct modules importing a common assignment also shared an override. Context-bearing ASTs are cached solely by file path.

item: User-defined functions discard evaluation state
note: Reproduced ignored overrides, three executions of one backtick assignment, parameter capture of a global dependency, missing exported values, and true/false is_dependency disagreement. Functions construct a fresh evaluator.

item: Relative and unnormalized search ceilings are ignored
note: Both --ceiling . and an absolute path containing child/../child ran the parent recipe. The normalized absolute ceiling stopped searching. Project-root discovery uses the same unnormalized comparison.

item: Formatting drops alias privacy
note: Formatting removed the alias's private attribute, making the previously hidden alias appear in --list. Alias serialization omits its attributes.

item: Formatting drops module privacy
note: Formatting removed module privacy, exposing the module and its recipes in listings. Module serialization ignores its private field; this is separate from alias serialization.

item: Strict Clippy fails on the supplied toolchain
note: Reproduced manual_assert_eq and four assert_is_empty diagnostics, including one integration-test occurrence. Allowing both lints passed. These are assertion-style lint failures, not correctness defects.

item: Strict private-item rustdoc fails on Markdown
note: Reproduced one unresolved link and three undefined-footnote errors with private items and warnings denied. Public documentation passed. This is documentation/build cleanliness.

item: Shell evaluation output adds backslashes to exclamation marks
note: Shell-format output escaped ! inside double quotes. Loading that output with both sh and bash preserved the added backslash, changing the value. The existing test asserts the incorrect emitted text.

item: Cross-module aliases disappear or receive unrelated signatures
note: An executable cross-module alias was absent from default and separate listings. Adding a same-named local target made the alias appear with that unrelated recipe's parameters.

item: Root lazy setting controls child-module evaluation
note: A lazy child under an eager root executed its unused failing assignment. An eager child under a lazy root skipped it. The root computes one reference filter for every module, contrary to independent module settings.

item: Settings analysis evaluates unused assertions
note: An unused failing assertion blocked an unrelated recipe under set lazy, selective --evaluate good, and --list. Settings analysis evaluates every assignment and propagates assertion errors.

item: Variable cycles through functions abort the process
note: The claimed stack-exhaustion abort was not tested because resource-exhaustion investigations are explicitly excluded. No recursive execution probe was attempted.

item: Sync userdata shared borrows become exclusive with send
note: Overlapping String borrows return UserDataBorrowError; existing send and wrapper tests fail. Extracted detector returns false for String/u64 on stable and nightly, debug and optimized.

note: Lua 5.4 weak-value regression retains the cleared table after dropping its handle and collecting twice; untouched control is collected. Luau control passes. Non-Luau code lacks stack restoration.

note: On Lua 5.4 and Luau, both conversion directions change {present:null,items:[null,1]} into {items:[1]}; default-option controls preserve it. The skip predicate includes null lightuserdata.

note: On Lua 5.4 and Luau, {1,2} equals [1,2,3] and an empty table equals [1]. Equal-length and shorter-slice controls behave correctly; the final return omits the length check.

item: Numeric sets fail their own round-trip conversion
note: HashSet<i32> and BTreeSet<i32> containing 1,2,3 fail with boolean-to-i32 errors on Lua 5.4 and Luau; string-set control passes. Membership tables are misclassified as sequences, also at line 1102.

item: Tuple variants omit the array metatable
note: Default serialization of an empty tuple variant produces {Empty:{}} instead of {Empty:[]} on Lua 5.4 and Luau. Tuple-variant table creation bypasses the enabled array-metatable option.

item: Nil fields shift subsequent tuple-variant fields
note: With serialize_none_to_null(false), Items(None,7) stores 7 at index 1 on Lua 5.4 and Luau; the ordinary-tuple control keeps it at index 2. raw_push recomputes the insertion index after nil.

item: Failed Luau vector-to-array conversion omits destructors
note: A custom conversion accepts component 1 and rejects component 2: the destructor count is zero for a vector, one for the table control. MaybeUninit elements have no cleanup guard on early return.

item: Luau buffer relative seeks overflow before validation
note: Debug tests panic on End(i64::MAX) and on Current(i64::MAX) from position 1 in a three-byte buffer. Ordinary invalid-seek control returns Err; release behavior was not tested.

item: Documentation links to disabled async APIs
note: Strict baseline rustdoc fails on three async links at lines 42-44; enabling async removes those diagnostics. This is documentation/build hygiene.

item: Documentation cannot resolve the sandbox link
note: Normal expanded-feature docs warn that Lua is not in scope for Lua::sandbox; -D warnings turns it into an error. This is a broken documentation reference.

item: Documentation Debug link is ambiguous
note: Normal docs warn that Debug names both a struct and derive macro; strict docs fail. Qualifying the link is documentation/build hygiene.

item: Path lookup rejects the minimum integer key
note: Lua 5.4 accepts the i64::MIN table key, but its bracket path returns integer overflow; adjacent-minimum and maximum controls pass. Positive signed accumulation overflows before negation.

item: Strict Clippy rejects redundant pointer casts on aarch64
note: Reproduced four unnecessary_cast diagnostics: conversion.rs:534/667, string.rs:133, util/mod.rs:279. Here c_char is u8; these casts do not change runtime behavior.

item: Strict Clippy rejects a redundant formatting borrow
note: Reproduced useless_borrows_in_formatting under -D warnings. The extra reference has no behavioral consequence.

item: Public documentation omits items and error sections
note: Independent advisory Clippy reproduces 22 missing_docs, 116 missing_errors_doc and one missing_panics_doc diagnostics. Representative source omissions are documentation housekeeping.

item: Public wrapper types lack Debug
note: Advisory Clippy reproduces 16 sites, including hidden helpers; source confirms exported Chunk, WeakLua, VmState and iterators lack Debug. This is optional public-API style, not a violated contract.

item: Unsafe operations lack local invariant comments
note: Advisory Clippy reproduces 180 undocumented_unsafe_blocks diagnostics; inspected transmute sites lack local rationale. This is comment/maintainability housekeeping; no runtime defect is claimed or established.

item: Userdata equality ignores metamethods across different metatables
note: Two userdata types with the first defining true __eq compare true in Lua 5.4 but false through Value::equals. The early metatable-inequality return contradicts the documented first/second lookup.

item: Metatable iteration converts restricted values before filtering
note: For empty userdata, visible Value entries are all strings, but pairs::<String>() errors converting a hidden boolean/function on Lua 5.4/Luau. TablePairs converts V before restricted keys are skipped.

item: Invalid table keys abort instead of returning errors
note: Separate Lua 5.4 tests for nil/NaN through set/raw_set and nil through create_table_from each terminate with SIGABRT. An 8 MiB limit control returns errors. Unprotected lua_rawset is also at state/raw.rs:575.

item: Mixed integer/float equality loses integer precision
note: Integer(9007199254740993) compares equal to Number(9007199254740992.0) through PartialEq and equals; Lua 5.4 returns false. Casting the integer to f64 erases the difference.

item: Fixed Serde tuples reject trailing unsupported values despite skipping
note: With deny_unsupported_types(false), {1,2,function() end} converts to Vec [1,2] but fails conversion to (i32,i32) with invalid length 3, on Lua 5.4 and Luau. Final validation bypasses skip logic.

item: Removing a thread hook retains its callback capture
note: Both main-thread and coroutine removal tests leave a captured Arc at strong count 2 after two collections. remove_hook only disables lua_sethook; it leaves the callback registry entry installed.

item: Boolean closing errors are inverted during thread reset
note: Resetting a yielded Lua 5.4 thread whose pending __close calls error(true) returns runtime error: false. The utility tests lua_toboolean != 1 instead of != 0.

item: Luau vector Serde accepts a tuple with too few components
note: A three-component vector succeeds as (f32,f32), while an equivalent table rejects the target and a three-element tuple succeeds. The vector branch never checks remaining components after the visitor.

item: Async compute releases serialization guard before committing
note: Independent single-thread regression paused an async eviction listener: three increments returned 1,2,2 and cached 2 instead of 3. The guard is consumed before insertion awaits. Baseline sync,future and all-feature suites passed.

item: Fallible unit-error initialization can panic an infallible caller
note: Independent sync and future regressions made get_with wait behind try_get_with returning Err(()). Both reached internal unreachable! panics. Their waiter identities use the same unit TypeId.

item: Expiry update returning None retains an elapsed deadline
note: Both cache variants returned None after replacing an expired value whose update callback returned None. checked_duration_since converts the elapsed deadline to None, and the equality shortcut leaves the old timestamp stored.

note: In both variants, invalidate_all made get return None, but remove returned Some(42). Compute callbacks received None yet Op::Remove returned Removed(42), contradicting the documented StillNone result.

item: Generation wraparound prevents maintenance and eviction
note: Mocked-clock regressions in both variants ran maintenance after every replacement. Invalidation removed the entry after 65,534 replacements but retained it after 65,535. Numeric ordering rejects the wrapped generation; eviction paths skip dirty entries.

item: Public example links break strict documentation builds
note: Strict public rustdoc reproduced unresolved try_append_value_async.rs links at lines 201 and 743. The definitions instead name the synchronous example. Documentation/build hygiene.

item: Private Arc documentation has an unresolved ptr::eq link
note: Strict rustdoc with private items reproduced the unresolved link because ptr is not imported. Qualifying std::ptr::eq addresses this documentation warning.

item: Private Arc documentation contains a bare URL
note: Strict private-item rustdoc reproduced rustdoc::bare_urls. This is hyperlink formatting and warning cleanliness.

item: Unsafe operations lack local invariant comments
note: Advisory Clippy reproduced 77 unsafe-block and 13 unsafe-implementation comment warnings. Representative operations lack local explanations; these documentation omissions do not establish an operational defect.

item: Public API items lack documentation
note: Advisory checking reproduced 23 missing-item documentation warnings within src. Both and_try_compute_if_nobody_else methods lack documentation. This is documentation hygiene.

item: Result-returning APIs lack formal Errors sections
note: Advisory Clippy reproduced 20 missing-Errors-section warnings. Several APIs already explain error behavior in prose; the asserted omission concerns documentation structure.

note: The missing_debug_implementations lint identified two builders, four entry selectors, and two iterators, matching the reports. Adding diagnostic formatting is public-API hygiene.

item: Borrowed-key fallible entry hits omit the key
note: Independent sync and segmented-cache tests retrieved the existing value, then key() panicked with Bug: Key is None. The future-cache control passed. Source hardcodes need_key=false; Debug also calls key().

item: Reordered weighted updates permanently distort accounting
note: Paused the update to weight 2 while weight 3 completed first. Both variants then reported weight 4 for their sole weight-3 value; removing it left an empty cache reporting weight 1. Saturating deltas lose accounting information.

note: Both variants replaced 10 with 20 through or_insert_with_if, but returned is_old_value_replaced=false. The initializer result constructs Entry with a hardcoded false despite the documented flag contract.

note: An ordinary mocked-clock regression cleared expiry through an unrecorded conditional-entry read, advanced maintenance, and observed timer_node still set after its node was dropped. item: Trybuild snapshots mismatch the installed compiler diagnostics
note: Executed the cfg(trybuild) suite: both test functions failed across three snapshots. Actual programs still produced the expected Clone-bound errors; differences were diagnostic spans and formatting on Rust 1.99.1.

item: getopts-only configuration cannot build the binary
note: Reproduced E0432 with --no-default-features --features getopts; adding --lib passes. The binary requires getopts but imports feature-gated html unconditionally.

item: CLI ignores stdin read errors
note: Invalid UTF-8 stdin produced empty output, no diagnostic, and exit 0. The read_to_string result is discarded.

item: CLI loses output errors and buffered flush failures
note: Both /dev/full and a closed stdout pipe produced exit 0 without diagnostics. Rendering errors are discarded, and the BufWriter has no checked explicit flush.

item: CLI panics on missing input files
note: A nonexistent filename triggers expect and exits 101 with a panic diagnostic. Failure is detectable, but ordinary file-open errors use panic handling.

item: CLI repeats earlier files during batch conversion
note: Alpha and Beta files rendered Alpha once, then Alpha and Beta together. read_to_string appends to the reused input buffer before each rendering.

item: CRLF becomes two spaces inside code spans
note: `a\r\nb` rendered code text containing two spaces; the blockquote variant did too. The code-span loop replaces CR and LF separately.

item: Trailing tabs prevent code fences from closing
note: Reproduced with backtick and tilde fences: the closing fence and following paragraph remain code. The scanner consumes trailing spaces only; bundled CommonMark permits tabs.

note: ASCII and Unicode case variants resolve in the parser but render different targets and numbers. FOO targets #FOO although only id="foo" exists; numbering uses case-sensitive strings.

note: Reproduced malformed indented-code, fenced-code, HTML-block, and heading-attribute parsing with CR-only input. scan_nextline searches only for LF, contrary to the bundled line-ending contract.

note: 499 é and 249 crab characters resolve, while 500 é, 250 crabs, and 334 CJK characters fail. A 1000-character ASCII label resolves. The counter increments for non-ASCII bytes rather than Unicode characters.

item: Wikilink source ranges omit the final bracket
note: [[Wiki]] reports link ranges 0..7 instead of 0..8. Piped wikilinks and wiki images also omit the last byte; handle_wikilink assigns end_ix + 1.

note: [[Wiki|]] renders ]]. Empty-alias handling selects a closing-bracket node as display content.

note: # heading {a bb c=d} drops a while retaining bb and c. The parser applies attr.len() > 1 to all attributes, although documented custom attributes have no such restriction.

item: Literal NUL is retained instead of normalized
note: Ordinary regression input a\0b retained NUL in rendered HTML instead of U+FFFD, contrary to bundled CommonMark. Verification concerned text normalization only.

item: SIMD functions lack complete written safety contracts
note: The cited comments omit some preconditions and the unsafe call lacks a SAFETY explanation. This establishes documentation housekeeping; no invalid access is claimed or established. No dedicated safety investigation was performed.

item: Tabbed fence metadata enters the language class
note: rust\tcustom produces class="language-rust\tcustom", while space-separated metadata is excluded. The renderer splits only on literal spaces; this is a renderer-consistency issue, not a mandated CommonMark rendering rule.

item: Public API documentation omissions
note: Reproduced 65 library missing-documentation warnings and two missing # Errors sections. BrokenLink fields lack documentation, including span units. These are documentation omissions without a demonstrated behavioral defect.

item: Smart-punctuation documentation gives the wrong double-hyphen replacement
note: Documentation says -- becomes an em dash. Executed a -- --- produced an en dash followed by an em dash, confirming the example is incorrect.

item: Strict Clippy fails on the supplied toolchain
note: Reproduced four build-script diagnostics with all features and 23 library diagnostics with serde,simd under -D warnings. These are lint-cleanliness failures; ordinary builds and package tests pass.

item: HTML blocks reject valid closing tags
note: Uppercase matching closers and a different permitted closing tag both leave following Markdown inside the HTML block. Termination uses a case-sensitive search for one specific closing tag; CommonMark permits any listed closer case-insensitively.

item: Tabs are mishandled around ATX closing hashes
note: Tabs before or after closing hashes leave literal hashes in headings. The trimming and preceding-whitespace checks recognize spaces only, despite CommonMark allowing tabs.

item: Inline link titles are accepted without a separator
note: [a](<url>"title") emitted a link with destination url and title title. The whitespace-separated control also works; the parser never requires the separator mandated when destination and title are both present.

item: Carets and tildes incorrectly share delimiter-search bounds
note: Enabling subscript cancels superscript in ^a b~ c^; enabling superscript cancels strikethrough in ~~a b^ c~~. Both regressions share the same TILDES lower-bound slot for carets and tildes.

item: Wrapping a wiki image in a link corrupts its destination
note: [![[foo.png]]](bar) rendered an unlinked image with src="bar" and alt="](bar)". Stale ordinary bracket-stack entries allow subsequent link handling to overwrite the wiki image.

item: Subscript-only mode suppresses ordinary inline parsing
note: With only ENABLE_SUBSCRIPT, double tildes cause enclosed emphasis, links, and code spans to render literally. Unsupported delimiter pairs become Text nodes with children that event traversal skips.

item: Tabs incorrectly count toward hard line breaks
note: Two tabs, space-tab, and tab-space before a newline each produced br. The implementation counts non-newline ASCII whitespace rather than the literal trailing spaces required by CommonMark.

item: Tabs fail to terminate unquoted HTML attribute values
note: a z escaped the valid opening tag while retaining the closing tag. The unquoted-value predicate excludes spaces and line endings but omits tabs.

item: Internal colons are accepted in table delimiter cells
note: A delimiter row containing -:- produced a right-aligned table. Bundled GFM permits colons only at delimiter-cell edges; the scanner allows hyphens after a trailing alignment colon.

item: Generated suites do not exercise subscript in isolation
note: Accurate coverage context: the helper always enables strikethrough alongside optional subscript. Independently reran existing suites successfully: default 1255, all-features 1260, no-default-features 79 tests. The isolated parsing defect is recorded separately.

item: Disabling server configuration panics on pending connections
note: Connection simulations panicked at :211 on a duplicate Initial and :540 on accepting the pending Incoming after set_server_config(None).

item: Rejected ordered read discards receive state
note: Read abc unordered from abcdef, received IllegalOrderedRead, then received ClosedStream instead of def. The error path drops the removed receive state.

item: ACK-delay clamp panics with valid peer minimum
note: Parameter decoding accepted minimum/maximum delays of 100 ms. Calculating the requested delay at RTT 10 ms panicked because clamp received inverted bounds.

item: Optional integer transport parameters panic on decoding errors
note: Parsing 20 00 panicked on UnexpectedEnd instead of returning Err. Both optional-integer branches unwrap decoding without restricting it to the declared value length.

item: STOP then RESET returns receive credit twice
note: With a 100-byte window and 32 unread bytes, stopping raised local_max_data to 132; the matching reset incorrectly raised it again to 164.

item: Window restoration fails to cancel shrink debt
note: Changing an unused receive window from 100 to 50 to 100 produced local_max_data=150. Expansion grants credit while retaining shrink debt.

item: Zero minimum MTU change prevents search completion
note: With minimum_change(0), 32 successful component-search iterations still proposed 1451 within [1451,1452]. The stopping comparison cannot become true.

item: Failed connection creation retains provisional CID routing state
note: Connecting with an invalid server name returned InvalidServerName with zero connections but one known CID. Registration precedes fallible session creation without rollback.

item: Transport parameters reject valid wider integer encodings
note: Canonical 04 01 01 decoded successfully; equivalent 04 02 40 01 failed. The parser compares length against the value's minimum encoding size.

item: Datagram eviction excludes the incoming length
note: With a four-byte send buffer, queuing aaaa then bbbb with dropping enabled delivered aaaa first. Eviction checks only the preexisting queued byte count.

item: TLS-version compatibility is not checked during conversion
note: With rustls/tls12 enabled, a TLS-1.2-only client configuration converted successfully, then connect panicked at :366. Documentation promises TLS 1.3 is required for conversion to succeed.

item: Unsupported server early-data size panics during session creation
note: The 1024-byte configuration converted and later panicked as reported, but :425 and :465 explicitly require a QUIC server early-data size of 0 or u32::MAX. This example violates a documented configuration precondition.

item: Qlog RTT metrics use seconds instead of milliseconds
note: With qlog enabled, four 100 ms RTT durations became [Some(0.1);4] instead of [Some(100.0);4], making exported recovery durations 1000 times too small.

item: CID validation panics on short IDs
note: Validating a constructible empty ConnectionId panicked at split_at(3). The public fallible validator documents no minimum length; source establishes the same failure for lengths 1 and 2.

item: Safe StreamId construction can violate VarInt bounds
note: Index 1<<60 constructed a StreamId converting to VarInt(4611686018427387906), above MAX. Encoding also panicked at :301. The constructor accepts the unrestricted index.

item: Explicit endpoint RNG seed still calls OS entropy
note: Option::map_or eagerly evaluates StdRng::from_os_rng even with a seed, contradicting rng_seed's entropy-free-environment contract. The dependency documents panic on entropy failure; no failure was injected.

item: Default public rustdoc contains a feature-disabled verifier link
note: Strict default rustdoc failed on with_platform_verifier; enabling its feature resolves the link. This is documentation/build cleanliness.

item: Private rustdoc contains a feature-disabled qlog link
note: Strict default rustdoc with private items failed on QlogStream. Documentation passed with qlog and platform-verifier enabled. This is documentation/build cleanliness.

item: Datagram capability query ignores local disablement
note: With local datagrams disabled and peer support enabled, send returned Disabled while max_size returned Some(1414), contradicting its documented None result.

item: Public error and panic documentation gaps
note: The stream accessors assert direction requirements without documenting those panics. Missing Errors/Panics sections and advisory lint totals are documentation hygiene, not additional runtime defects.

item: Public types lack Debug implementations
note: TokenReuseError and representative public types lack Debug; Result::expect requires Debug for its error. Adding diagnostic traits is API-style housekeeping. Exact reported totals were not independently counted.

item: Unchecked VarInt conversions lack invariant explanations
note: The four cited calls lack adjacent explanations of the required 62-bit bound. Comments would improve maintenance; the concrete StreamId bounds failure is assessed separately.

item: Strict Clippy flags a manually implemented enum default
note: Baseline strict Clippy reproduced derivable_impls on Rust 1.99.1. Deriving Default is a lint/style transformation, not a behavior defect.

item: Strict Clippy flags manual Option filtering
note: Baseline strict Clippy reproduced manual_filter on Rust 1.99.1. Replacing the equivalent expression is lint/style housekeeping.

item: Rejected 0-RTT retains discarded send-window charges
note: A resumption/rejection simulation filled a 13-byte send window. After handshake success, resending on the replacement stream returned Blocked. zero_rtt_rejected leaves unacked_data charged.

item: Stopping a reset stream fails to advertise replacement stream credit
note: With one permitted incoming stream, an empty RESET followed by accept and stop left the peer unable to open another stream after driving both endpoints. stop omits queue_max_stream_id.

item: Zero idle timeout rejects immediate server acceptance
note: A server configured with Some(IdleTimeout(0)) rejected an immediately accepted valid Initial with TimedOut. The staleness check treats disabled timeout zero as an immediate deadline.

item: BBR bandwidth maximum never expires lower samples
note: After measuring 1000000 bytes/s and then 28 rounds at 100000 bytes/s, the estimate remained 1000000. Lower samples never reach the ten-round maximum filter.

item: MTU datagram pruning drops payloads equal to the limit
note: drop_oversized(5) removed a queued five-byte payload and reduced outgoing_total to zero. The retain predicate uses < although the contract discards only larger payloads.

item: Connection credit exhaustion hides a stopped-stream write error
note: With 100 bytes of connection credit consumed across two streams, STOP_SENDING(42) made stopped() return Some(42), but another write returned Blocked instead of Stopped(42).

item: RESET then STOP returns receive credit twice
note: For 32 unread bytes in a 100-byte window, RESET raised local_max_data to 132; subsequent stop incorrectly raised it to 164. Recv::stop credits bytes already discarded by reset.

item: Path MTU reset leaves an oversized datagram blocking the queue
note: After payload capacity fell from 1414 to 1162 on a new 1200-byte link, driving the connection delivered no small datagram queued behind the old large one. The small-only control passed.

item: NEON vector store assumes allocation alignment
note: Existing get_nested test under Miri fails: pointer alignment 8, required 16. Offset modulo four does not establish Vec<u32> allocation alignment.

item: Typed tape getters truncate containers
note: All four getters reproduce truncation. [1,2] iterates only 1; empty containers panic on len(); nested arrays panic during iteration. Slice lengths omit the header.

item: Numeric deserialization reads beyond exhausted tape
note: The second safe u64::deserialize call after reading 1 panics with an out-of-bounds index. Numeric helpers call unchecked next_ without checking EOF; release behavior was not executed.

item: 128bit plus approximate parsing cannot compile
note: Capped cargo check fails on missing static_cast_i128 at approx.rs:339. Its gates name nonexistent i128, and approx.rs lacks its import. Nightly all-features also fails.

item: Approximate parsing without SWAR cannot compile
note: Capped cargo check --no-default-features --features approx-number-parsing fails E0432: unconditional imports reference helpers gated behind swar-number-parsing.

item: big-int-as-float regression test does not compile
note: Feature tests fail E0277 comparing OwnedValue with StaticNode. Library-only cargo check succeeds. Both commands used the lint cap.

item: Huge-integer regression input fits the 128bit range
note: The thirty-digit input is below u128::MAX. With 128bit it exercises integer parsing rather than overflow-to-float, even after repairing the comparison type.

item: Pretty tuple variants omit closing delimiters
note: Pair(1,2) leaves its array open; Empty() lacks the outer object delimiter. serde_json rejects both outputs. Source also confirms incomplete indentation restoration.

item: Unknown-length empty containers serialize incompletely
note: Empty serialize_seq(None) returns Ok("[") in compact and pretty modes; pretty serialize_map(None) returns Ok("{"). The first flag conflates empty and already closed.

item: Serde visitors do not enforce container consumption
note: Deserializing [[1,2],3] as ((u8,),u8) returns Ok(((1,),2)), replacing the sibling value. Tuple length is ignored and visitor consumption is unchecked.

item: Exponent narrowing wraps large magnitudes
note: 1e4294967296 and 1e-4294967296 both become 1.0; neighboring exponents produce 10.0 and 0.1. The accumulated exponent is narrowed to i32 without validation.

item: Slow numeric paths bypass terminator validation
note: Large integer and long fractional tokens ending in x are accepted, including inside arrays. [123x] correctly errors. Slow conversion returns precede delimiter validation.

item: Missing low-surrogate escape becomes NUL
note: "\ud800" becomes NUL and "\ud800x" becomes NUL followed by x. Missing second escape returns Ok((0,6)) instead of an error.

item: Second surrogate lacks an upper-bound check
note: "\ud800\ue000" becomes U+10400 and "\udbff\uffff" becomes U+10FFFF. Valid boundary pairs pass. checked_sub rejects values below DC00 but accepts values above DFFF.

item: Consuming DOM conversion rejects numeric map keys
note: Owned and borrowed consuming conversions to BTreeMap<u32,String> reject key "42"; both reference conversions succeed. Consuming ObjectAccess uses ordinary string-value deserialization.

item: BorrowedValue map keys lack an owned fallback
note: Deserialization through serde_json fails for escaped keys and owned Value objects, expecting a borrowed string. visit_map requests &str despite supporting owned string storage.

item: Tape scalar methods lose wide integers
note: With 128bit, tape access returns None for unsigned 18446744073709551616 and signed -9223372036854775809. Equivalent DOM access succeeds. Tape inherits defaults that use narrower accessors.

item: Tape conversion tests exercise StaticNode instead
note: The test module aliases StaticNode as Value. Its 128-bit conversion assertions construct that alias and cannot detect missing tape scalar forwarding.

item: Lazy equality changes after representation upgrade
note: Equal clones of {"a":1} become unequal after as_object_mut() on one without modifying entries. Derived PartialEq distinguishes Tape and Value variants.

item: Strict checks fail on the supplied newer compiler
note: Uncapped Clippy reproduces three unused-import errors and manual_is_multiple_of. Capped default tests pass (464 tests). This is the supplied compiler compatibility limit; Rust 1.88 was not tested.

item: Lint allows lack reason attributes
note: Independent advisory Clippy finds 69 distinct allow locations without reasons. This is lint-policy housekeeping.

item: Unsafe operations lack recognized safety comments
note: Advisory Clippy reproduces missing-comment diagnostics, including two unsafe implementations. Mechanical comment recognition does not establish additional correctness defects.

item: Public container and buffer types lack Debug
note: Independent advisory Clippy identifies 13 public types. Adding Debug is public-API style and diagnostic convenience.

item: Long decimal values depend on byte offset
note: After 64 spaces, 1.2345678901234567890123456789 becomes 5.097733592125637e-10. Reproduced with default and 128bit features. start_digits stores an ASCII byte instead of a position.

item: Nonfinite floats serialize as invented numbers
note: Compact, pretty and DOM encoding turn NaN into 2.696539702293474e308 and infinity into 1.797693134862316e308. Nonfinite values reach ryu format_finite without validation.

item: Serde float deserialization omits 128-bit nodes
note: With 128bit, deserializing 18446744073709551616 into f64 returns ExpectedFloat despite exact representability. parse_double handles only F64, I64 and U64; f32 shares this path.

item: Malformed literals are classified as data errors
note: falsex, truex and nullx produce ExpectedFalse/True/Null with is_syntax()==false and is_data()==true, contradicting the documented classification.

item: Unexpected error equality is not reflexive
note: Unexpected(Some(String),Some(Bool)) compares unequal to itself. PartialEq omits Unexpected and falls through to false.

item: Escaped-object aliasing observation is model-dependent
note: Reproduced a Stacked Borrows retag failure. After isolating it with unaligned stores in scratch, Tree Borrows passes. Experimental-model disagreement leaves a language-level defect unsettled.

item: ZIP64 offsets are not regenerated on append, merge or deep copy
note: Sparse-file regressions: original entry reads correctly; append and merge make it unreadable; deep-copy destination resolves to the original header. Serialization reuses stripped or stale ZIP64 extra data.

item: Rewriting Implode entries drops decoding flags
note: Existing implode.zip reads before rewriting. Append, merge and raw copy discard compression-specific flags and subsequently fail to decode.

item: Raw copy loses ZipCrypto encryption state
note: Untouched by_index_raw copy succeeds but encrypted() becomes false and reading fails checksum. Original entry decrypts correctly.

item: Raw copy accepts readers whose required bytes were consumed
note: Fresh decrypted AES reader copies successfully but output rejects its password. Reading one byte from a Deflate entry before copying also produces unreadable output. Untouched raw AES control passes.

item: Raw copy discards file kind, comments and extra fields
note: Regressions show a symlink becomes a regular file, custom 0xbeef extra data disappears, and a file comment becomes empty. SimpleFileOptions reconstruction omits this metadata.

item: finish_into_readable retains ZIP64 sentinel sizes
note: Five-byte Stored entry reports both sizes as 4294967295; reading returns 94 bytes including directory data, then Invalid checksum. Serializing and reopening reads the five bytes correctly.

item: finish_into_readable retains AES wire compression marker
note: Returned archive rejects correct-password access with unsupported compression. Equivalent finish followed by ZipArchive::new decrypts successfully.

item: Unicode comment checksum uses decoded comment bytes
note: Valid CP437 comment with Unicode-field CRC over original bytes prevents opening: Could not find EOCD. ASCII control and Python reads pass. Source validates decoded UTF-8 bytes instead.

item: Oversized filenames panic and abort during cleanup
note: 65535-byte boundary succeeds; 65536-byte name panics at unchecked u16 conversion. Standalone cleanup triggers another panic at types.rs:934 and SIGABRT. Input exceeds ZIP filename capacity.

item: Appending long CP437 comments aborts during cleanup
note: Valid archive with a 40000-byte CP437 comment opens, but append finish unwraps its expanded UTF-8 length conversion. Standalone process panics twice and terminates with SIGABRT.

item: Stream boundary handling loses metadata and rejects empty archives
note: Two-entry visitor succeeds with two file callbacks and zero metadata callbacks; empty archive returns UnexpectedEof. Parser consumes 30 bytes before recognizing central header, then metadata errors are suppressed. Existing tests never require callbacks.

item: Extraction skips restoring directory permissions
note: Linux regression archives directory mode 0500 and extracts it as 0755. Directory branch continues before adding its mode to the restoration queue.

item: Seekable entry API returns encrypted payload bytes
note: Stored ZipCrypto hello requires a password through by_index, but by_name_seek succeeds and returns 17 encrypted bytes. Seek path checks compression without checking encryption.

item: Path lookup cannot retrieve directory entries
note: Directory created with add_directory_from_path(dir/subdir/) is found by_name with its slash, but by_path of the same path returns FileNotFound because normalization removes that slash.

item: Streamed data_start accessor panics
note: Ordinary streamed entry panics on data_start(): OnceLock remains unset and accessor unwraps it, despite documentation promising zero.

item: Stream raw copies omit required data descriptors
note: Raw-copy stream output sets bit 3 but emits no descriptor; ordinary streamed-file control emits one. Central-directory reads still work. writing_raw skips descriptor finalization.

item: Stream directory entries omit required data descriptors
note: Stream directory output sets bit 3 and emits no descriptor. add_directory clears writing_to_file, bypassing descriptor finalization.

item: Access-only timestamps become modification timestamps
note: Local field flags=2, length=5, timestamp=42 produces mod_time=Some(42), ac_time=None. Five-byte heuristic overrides the timestamp flags.

item: Documented Bzip2 default disagrees with actual default
note: With only bzip2 enabled, default-options output uses Stored. Documentation explicitly promises Bzip2 in this configuration.

item: Strict Clippy reports collapsible_match
note: Reproduced on Rust 1.99.1. Allowing this single lint makes strict all-feature/all-target Clippy pass. Lint cleanliness does not establish incorrect behavior.

item: Rustdoc contains unresolved links
note: Strict rustdoc reproduces five broken links including private items and six without default features. Four concern public all-feature documentation. These are documentation housekeeping issues.

item: Empty XZ entries contain invalid compressed data
note: Ordinary empty-XZ round-trip fails with index CRC32 mismatch under locked lzma-rust2 0.13.0. Nonempty XZ control reads correctly.

item: Streaming ZipCrypto uses wrong password verification byte
note: Fixed-timestamp streamed entry finishes successfully but rejects its correct password. Writer uses CRC byte; descriptor-flagged reader expects modification-time byte.

item: Zopfli-only low compression levels panic
note: With only deflate-zopfli, levels 1, 6 and 8 panic on subtraction, and 9 on zero NonZeroU64 conversion. Levels 0/265 return errors; 10/264 succeed. Validation admits levels below documented minimum.

item: Append rewrites CP437 comments with wrong encoding flag
note: Fixture comment café becomes caf├⌐ after append. Writer emits UTF-8 comment bytes while deriving encoding flags only from the ASCII filename.

item: ZIP64 comments disappear on small archives
note: set_zip64_comment(Some(hello)) reopens with None. Writer emits ZIP64 footer, but ZIP32 fields lack the sentinels required by reader detection.

item: Central-directory I/O failures lose original error
note: Injected I/O failure during the 46-byte central-header parse becomes InvalidArchive(Could not find EOCD), rather than ZipError::Io. Candidate backtracking discards the original error.

item: Public failure contracts omit Errors sections
note: Representative Result-returning APIs omit formal Errors headings. Missing documentation and advisory counts do not establish additional behavior defects.

item: Public reader and writer types lack Debug
note: Source confirms ZipFile, ZipFileSeek and StreamWriter lack Debug. Diagnostic convenience and derive support are public-API style housekeeping.

item: Unsafe byte-casting sites lack local safety explanations
note: Pod documents representation requirements; casting blocks and packed integer implementations lack local justifications. No production undefined behavior was established. Local comments are maintainability hygiene.

item: Lint suppressions lack structured reasons
note: Source contains allow attributes without reason arguments, sometimes with explanatory comments. Preference for reason/expect is housekeeping; no harmful stale suppression was demonstrated.

item: Advertised docs.rs configuration uses removed nightly feature
note: Advertised --cfg docsrs command fails on installed nightly with E0557: doc_auto_cfg was removed in Rust 1.92. Ordinary documentation builds do not enable this obsolete feature.

item: Streaming large_file rejects valid large compressed sizes
note: large_file selects the ZIP64 descriptor branch, but that branch rejects compressed_size above u32::MAX. Therefore a Stored 4 GiB entry is rejected despite enabling ZIP64. No large workload run.

item: Streaming ZIP64 central fields retain zero size placeholders
note: start_entry serializes zero ZIP64 sizes. Streaming finalization writes descriptors without updating that extra field; central serialization reuses it. Overflowing size sentinels consequently parse as zero. No multi-gigabyte workload run.

item: Extraction rejects ordinary links within destination
note: Ordinary real/, link -> real, link/file extraction fails with Invalid base path. Canonical absolute base reaches simplified_components, which rejects RootDir. Existing extracted links encounter the same branch.

item: Stale optional Unicode path rejects primary filename
note: Valid primary filename with stale optional Unicode metadata fails opening with Could not find EOCD; Python reads its payload. Source propagates optional-field CRC failure instead of falling back to the primary name.

item: Append serializes AES central method as underlying method
note: No-op append changes final central-directory method from 99 to 0 while local method remains 99. Serializer writes the parsed underlying method instead of AES wire method 99.

item: Documented Deflate compression level zero is rejected
note: Deflated level 0 returns UnsupportedArchive despite documented 0..9 range. Validation starts at Compression::fast(), whose level is 1.

item: Non-UTF-8 regression test violates String invariant
note: write_non_utf8 supplies invalid GB18030 and Shift-JIS bytes to String::from_utf8_unchecked, violating its UTF-8 precondition. Passing execution cannot validate this test. No production unsoundness inference is required.

item: Large capacity reservations truncate to zero
note: Probe observed capacity change from 1 to 0 after reserve_capacity(1usize << 32). Reserving 65,535 received capacity. The usize-to-u32 cast silently cancels demand.

item: 304 responses fail when completed by empty DATA
note: 304 with content-length: 100 followed by empty END_STREAM DATA produced PROTOCOL_ERROR. The same response ending in HEADERS succeeded. Representation length incorrectly remains required body length.

item: Pushed HEAD requests lose HEAD response semantics
note: A pushed HEAD response with content-length: 100 and END_STREAM failed with PROTOCOL_ERROR; omitting Content-Length succeeded. Promise reception never initializes ContentLength::Head.

item: Window setters omit bounds and panic documentation
note: All four cited client/server setters assert the 31-bit bound without documenting their panic conditions. This is documentation hygiene concerning invalid arguments, rather than a valid-input correctness defect.

item: Strict Clippy checks fail
note: Independently reproduced eight Clippy errors under -D warnings on Rust 1.99.1. These are style/representation diagnostics. Build, formatting, library, integration and all-feature tests passed; integration had 173 passing tests, contrary to B/C's 273.

item: Strict rustdoc rejects two bare URLs
note: Strict private-item documentation failed on bare URLs at decoder.rs:508 and headers.rs:959. Ordinary documentation built successfully. These are documentation lint omissions.

item: Header lists exactly at the configured maximum are rejected
note: A sole :status: 200 response failed with PROTOCOL_ERROR at limit 42 and succeeded at 43. Both pseudo-header and regular-field comparisons incorrectly exclude equality.

item: PUSH_PROMISE rejects an empty initial header fragment
note: A four-byte promised-stream ID followed by a valid CONTINUATION caused connection PROTOCOL_ERROR. Moving one header-block byte into PUSH_PROMISE succeeded. The loader incorrectly requires five bytes.

item: Outgoing trailers bypass header validation
note: send_trailers accepted connection: close, while the receiving codec rejected the emitted frame with PROTOCOL_ERROR. The send path closes the stream and queues trailers without check_headers.

item: Padded DATA loses flow-control credit
note: With an eight-byte stream window, one application byte plus seven padding-related bytes produced no WINDOW_UPDATE after release. An unpadded eight-byte control produced an eight-byte update. Accounting uses the stripped payload length.

item: Zero-byte writes are retried instead of returning WriteZero
note: A bounded transport returned zero once, then a sentinel error. Flushing performed the second write and returned the sentinel instead of WriteZero. The returned byte count is discarded; no unbounded test was performed.

item: Responses missing :status become successful 200 responses
note: A response header block containing only content-length: 0 completed successfully with status 200. convert_poll_message preserves Response::builder's default when the mandatory :status is absent.

item: Non-CONNECT authority-form requests are emitted without a scheme
note: send_request accepted GET example.com:443. The peer decoded an outgoing GET without :scheme. The applicable validation branch contains only a TODO instead of returning an error.

item: Rejected push requests retain reserved stream entries
note: The child stream is inserted and reserved before convert_push_message(...)? validates the request. Validation failure returns before unlink/remove. The store pointer has no automatic removal on drop, leaving the unused entry retained.

item: Shared module files conflate module identities
note: a::show printed b:default; invoking both modules executed once. Separate overrides produced only b:B. Separate source files correctly executed both recipes.

item: User-defined functions discard module bindings and overrides
note: Reproduced override:original, repeated assignment execution x:xx:xxx, different UUIDs, parameter-dependent reevaluation of globals, and missing exported variables in function backticks. Feature is unstable.

item: User-defined functions reset dependency status
note: A dependency printed true:false for direct is_dependency() versus its function wrapper; the directly invoked recipe printed false:false.

item: Invalid datetime formats panic
note: Invalid formats in both datetime functions and timestamp output exited 101 with a Display formatting panic. An external Rust caller confirmed all three unwind through just::run; ordinary function errors return Err(1).

item: Clippy rejects four assertion forms
note: Reproduced one manual_assert_eq and three assert_is_empty diagnostics on Rust 1.99.1. Allowing those two lints passes. This is lint cleanliness; the binary builds.

item: Lexer comments fail strict private rustdoc
note: Strict private documentation reproduced four link/footnote errors at lines 807, 824, 851 and 852. Strict public documentation passes. Documentation housekeeping.

item: shell() executes during dry runs
note: --dry-run created the shell() marker and printed the evaluated command. The equivalent backtick left its marker absent. This contradicts the documented preview behavior.

item: Dependency argument grouping can panic
note: The supplied declaration caused bar, --list and direct foo invocation to exit 101 in the default debug build. Removing the dependency restored foo. With debug assertions disabled, listing succeeds but bar returns an internal missing-parameter error.

item: Relative search ceilings are ignored
note: From the child directory, --ceiling . executed the parent's recipe. The equivalent absolute ceiling returned No justfile found. Config retains the relative path unchanged.

item: Quiet mode leaves script output visible
note: Both shebang and script-attribute recipes emitted stdout and stderr under --quiet. The linewise control suppressed both streams, matching the documented Suppress all output contract.

item: Formatting removes eager assignment semantics
note: With set lazy, an unused eager assignment created a marker before formatting. Formatting removed eager, and subsequent execution stopped creating the marker. The round-trip helper only checks successive dumps.

item: Formatting removes alias privacy
note: A private alias was absent from --list before formatting and appeared afterward. The alias serializer omits its attributes; this requires its own serialization fix.

item: Formatting removes module privacy
note: A private module was absent from --list before formatting and appeared afterward. The module serializer ignores private independently of alias serialization.

item: Multiline format strings are unindented twice
note: With two initial newlines, the format string without interpolation evaluated to hello followed by newline. Adding an empty interpolation preserved the additional leading newline, matching the ordinary string.

item: Shell evaluation output changes exclamation marks
note: Shell evaluation emitted x="hello\!" for hello!. Executing that output in both sh and bash produced hello\!, adding a literal backslash.

item: Common environment exports overwrite recipe attributes
note: Parameter-default backticks observed recipe while command bodies observed dotenv in linewise, shebang and script recipes. A module-export control similarly produced default=recipe body=module.

item: Cross-module aliases are grouped with unrelated local recipes
note: An alias to child::task disappeared from --list. Adding a parameterless local task made the alias appear with that incorrect signature. Executing the alias still reached the parameterized child recipe.

item: Resolved alias display drops the target module path
note: --show and --usage displayed alias shortcut := task for a child::task target. The resolved alias Display implementation uses only target.name; fixing list grouping alone does not fix this output.

item: Async computations release serialization before committing
note: Independent public-API regression paused the first write; the second increment completed before it. Final value was 1 instead of 2. Both original test configurations nevertheless pass 229 tests, with seven ignored.

item: Generation wraparound breaks LRU eviction
note: Sync and future regressions retain the older key and evict the newer key after 65,536 writes. The sync 65,535-write control passes. The numeric comparison rejects the wrapping policy-generation update.

item: Mixed fallible and infallible initialization can panic
note: Overlapping try_get_with returning Err(()) and get_with panic at the reported unreachable branches in both implementations. Their waiter TypeIds collide.

item: Expiration update returning None can retain an elapsed deadline
